findings: Blocking: execute() launches the Python gate with PYTHONPATH pointing into the editable worktree. Python can execute worktree-supplied sitecustomize.py during startup, before launch_gate.py waits for G and before the parent durably records the process group. An agent-created startup module can therefore run commands or spawn processes outside the gate, reopening the crash/release race. Launch the trusted gate with Python isolated mode (-I), while preserving the intended environment for the eventual exec target. Add a regression test with a worktree sitecustomize.py sentinel proving that startup code cannot run before gate authorization.
requirements_checked: Static review of supplied source only; no tools or files accessed. Supplied test results were not independently executed.
Mutating Git operations now use execute(); however, Python startup bypasses its launch gate.
Review and pending approval are persisted atomically; legacy missing requests have idempotent recovery.
Outbox reconciliation validates exact event text and issue identity.
Applied the stated privileged-owner and unsandboxed-check boundaries; no future GUI, authentication, or production features required.
